messages:
laura: Heads up — after the routing policy tweak earlier today I'm seeing slow chart renders for EU users. p95 render +1.2s, a few LCP regressions.

deploy-bot: deploy routing-policy/v2 started by jing at 2026-03-21T22:10:12Z (canary 30%).

sam: Yep, telemetry shows a spike aligned with that rollout. Chart fetch latency and main-thread parse spikes.

anya: Looking at KV affinity metrics — lots of prefix cache misses. It looks like requests are getting routed to different GPU pools mid-session, so client-side cache keys become ineffective.

jing: We ramped the canary to 30% at 22:10, auto-roll to 100% at 22:40. I paused further ramps when we saw noise but maybe it already hit enough traffic.

mike: If routing is shuffling between pools, prefetch won't help because the KV keys are scoped to pool ids. We need sticky routing or shared keying.

laura: Quick triage idea: revert the final ramp and set routing-policy/v1 as default while we investigate. Or as a lighter mitigation, make client prefetch TTL longer so short re-routes don't drop cached prefixes.

sam: Rolling back to v1 is safest to remove customer impact. How quickly can we rollback?

jing: I can trigger rollback now. Note: there's a small schema diff to routing metadata in v2, but rolling back to v1 should be safe — no model changes.

laura: Thanks. Observability, please create a short-lived dashboard showing: p50/p95 chart render, KV cache hit ratio, routing churn by session-id, and bundle re-download count.

observability-bot: Created dashboard: /dashboards/console-rendering-regression-6165439876 (private) and alert: console.render.p95 > 800ms for 5m.

jing: Rolling back. Command: `/deploy rollback routing-policy v2 --to v1 --reason "console render regressions"`

deploy-bot: rollback started: routing-policy v2 -> v1 by jing at 2026-03-21T22:58:03Z. Canary set to 0%.

sam: After rollback start I'm already seeing p95 drop in EU in the telemetry feed (small sample). Will monitor for next 10m.

anya: For the long-term fix we should: 1) change KV cache keying to not include ephemeral pool id OR add cross-pool shared prefix layer; 2) add session stickiness header in the router; 3) add a canary gating metric that watches KV hit ratio and bundle re-downloads before full ramp.

mike: Agree. Also let's add a soft quota on prefetch concurrency per client so a misrouted prefetch flood doesn't swamp the new pool.

laura: I'll create a follow-up RFC for kvcache keying and canary gating. For now, add the temporary mitigation: extend client prefetch TTL to 30s and disable aggressive prefetch for widgets flagged as heavy (sparklines/heatmaps) — config flag `prefetch.heavy_threshold_ms`.

sam: Noted. I'll coordinate the telemetry keystones and add a canary health-check metric for future rollouts. :thumbsup:

laura: Thanks team. Postmortem follow-up: small incident doc later with timeline and actions.

mike: Quick note — save any heap/profile traces from affected sessions (client logs + sourcemap refs) before TTL changes roll out, else we lose the repro signal.

laura: Good call. Sam/anya can you snapshot current traces and export to the private s3 bucket?

anya: On it. Export started.

sam: Export done and linked in the dashboard notes.

laura: Closing loop here when the rollback fully finishes and p95 stays under 800ms for 30m.

observability-bot: Alert resolved at 2026-03-21T23:22:00Z (p95 back to baseline).
